correctness.rationale: For a scalar extension bounded in Lipschitz seminorm, constant reproduction forces the coefficients at a midpoint to sum to one, without requiring positivity; testing each vertex-distance function and summing gives S/(sum d_j) for the lower bound. Restricting to data on a fixed target line and applying a norm-one functional transfers this bound to any nonzero real Banach target. The cyclic sine recurrence has defect 4 sin(a) exactly at the zero chord, proving the inverse-distance identity, normalization and Dw=Lambda_n d. For positivity and monotonicity, u(theta)=sqrt(1+r^2-2r cos(theta)) satisfies u''+u/4=(1-r^2)^2/(4u^3)=F by differentiation; solving the forced oscillator over ±2a gives the stated convolution by the positive, even, nonincreasing circular kernel K, supported within distance 2a of zero. This proves positivity. To check the strict shell claim, for 0<=x<y<=pi pair the integration variables s with R(s)=x+y-s, modulo 2pi. On the open semicircle closer to x than y, cos(s)>cos(R(s)) since sin((x+y)/2)>0, so F(s)>F(R(s)); also K(s-x)>=K(s-y), strictly on a neighborhood of s=x. The paired convolution difference is strictly positive. The reverse shell recurrence for rho preserves 0<=rho_k<=2a_k by induction, using rho_q=a_q in the odd case (the opposite vertex's two adjacent masses are equal) and rho_q=0 in the even case. It yields w_j=(rho_j+rho_(j-1))/2 and unit total mass. For distinct midpoints, crossing the two endpoints makes the average chord cost exactly cos(a) times the corresponding vertex chord, including adjacent or antipodal centers; a common random rotation preserves this bound for the mixed laws. For vertex–midpoint pairs, Dw=Lambda_n d gives the required cost. The Banach triangle inequality transfers every coupling bound to the data. Strict convexity of the chord comparison at any other vertex gives Lambda_n>1; both normalized sums tend to 4/pi by uniform distance convergence and Riemann sums. An independent numerical check on n=3–120 corroborated weight and coupling identities; it is not an infinite certificate. The supplied script was read, not executed.
